resources.name: SAP Business One Service Layer (Insomnia)
resources.description:
Postman collection for the SAP Business One (B1) Service Layer REST APIs.

Generated from the [b1-api-cookbook](https://github.com/Xaypanya/b1-api-cookbook).

## Setup
1. Import the companion environment file `SAP-B1-ServiceLayer.postman_environment.json`.
2. Set `baseUrl` (e.g. `https://your-server:50000/b1s/v2`), `UserName`, `Password`, and `CompanyDB`.
3. Run the **00 - Authentication > Login** request first. The test script stores `B1SESSION` and `ROUTEID` automatically.
4. All other requests reuse those values via the `Cookie` header.

## Notes
- For self-signed SAP B1 certificates, disable SSL verification in Postman settings.
- Entity GET-by-id endpoints expect an id literal in the path (e.g. `BusinessPartners('C20000')`).

resources.name: Login
resources.description:
Log in Service Layer with the specified credentials. Generally it is the first step to using the Service Layer API. Calling the Service Layer API without a login will result in failure. After logging in successfully, one session ID will be returned in HTTP response body.
		At the same time, two HTTP cookie items named "B1SESSION" and "ROUTEID" will be set. You do not need to relate to them if calling the Service Layer API in a browser because the browser will send them to Service Layer automatically in subsequent HTTP requests. 
		You do need to add the cookie item "B1SESSION" to your HTTP header in a subsequent Service Layer API call. Otherwise, Service Layer will consider them as a bad request without a login. The cookie item "ROUTEID" is optional. It ensures the session stickiness and optimizes performance through efficient load balancing.

resources.name: POST Login
resources.description: Login Service Layer with the specified credentials.

resources.name: Logout
resources.description:
By default, a login session will expire and the user will be logged out automatically if there is no new request within 30 minutes. 
		You can change the default expire time by modifying the value of the "SessionTimeout" property in file "{USER_INSTALL_DIR}/ServiceLayer/conf/b1s.conf". 
		Here, "{USER_INSTALL_DIR}" stands for the installation folder.

resources.name: POST Logout
resources.description: Logout.
